title: Mahadev betting app still active, proceeds of crime exceed ₹92,000 cr: ED
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has told a court here that the illegal operations of the Mahadev online betting app and related money laundering activities were still continuing, and the  proceeds of crime were estimated to have exceeded Rs 92,000 crore.
The central agency on Friday sought seven-day custody of the alleged kingpin of the racket, Sourabh Chandrakar, from the special court for Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) cases.
His interrogation was necessary to unravel the money trail, identify the end use of the proceeds of crime and ascertain details of "betting panels" that are still operational, the ED said.
The court remanded Chandrakar in the ED's custody till November 19.
The ED said the revised proceeds of crime generated through the Mahadev Online Book application were estimated at Rs 75,000-80,000 crore, while those linked to its sister website Skyexchange.com stood at Rs 11,000-12,000 crore. The proceeds of crime linked to Lotus365.com were around Rs 2,400 .

title: No prosecution for previously-enrolled voters filing Form 6: EC to SC
content:
The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that voters whose names are missing from draft electoral rolls despite having been enrolled earlier can apply afresh through Form 6 without the fear of prosecution.
In an affidavit filed before the court, the poll panel said chief electoral officers have been requested to give wide publicity to the said clarification, in local languages as well.
"It had been brought to the notice of the Commission that some apprehensions were expressed that applicants who were enrolled as voters in previous electoral roll(s) but whose names did not appear in the draft Electoral Roll during the SIR -- by filing Form 6, may face action for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, on account of the fact that they were enrolled as voters in the previous electoral roll(s).
"In order to allay such misapprehensions, the Commission ... has clarified that no prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6

title: US air travel should recover from ground stop by end of Sunday, FAA says
content:
US air travel should be fully recovered from the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years by the end of Sunday, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said Saturday.
Bedford said the flights "will still have delays and cancellations" on Saturday but promised that the "worst is behind us."
His comments came as airlines across the US worked to recover from a ground stoppage that lasted four hours, stranding hundreds of thousands of passengers.
New technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated equipment and caused "intermittent" communications and radar gaps, leading to the flight shutdown of more than four hours, Trump administration officials said.
Planes were taking flight and landing Saturday, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said. But the effects could be felt for days. Officials say the system will likely return to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.

title: Air India says US flights operated as scheduled, with no major delays
content:
Air India on Saturday said all its flights to and from the US operated as scheduled without significant delays, even as thousands of flights were grounded across the country due to communications problems at regional air traffic control centres.
The airline also said in a statement that all its flights en route to New York, Newark and San Francisco landed on time early this morning.
The statement came after the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centres.
More than 2,500 flights were cancelled in the US on Saturday, and hundreds more were delayed, according to FlightAware, a website that tracks flight disruptions.
The FAA notice said the ground stop was imposed due to extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns.

title: Congress wants to contest 181 seats in 2027 UP polls, indicates Akhilesh
content:
Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav indicated on Saturday that the Congress has expressed its wish to contest 181 seats in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, while asserting that the INDIA bloc would remain united to defeat the ruling BJP in the state.
Asked at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in Delhi whether the Congress is seeking to contest 100 seats, Yadav said the party has demanded more than that. Asked if the demand was of 200 seats, he replied, "A little less than that." When the interviewer suggested 180 seats, Yadav said, "Add one more," indicating that the Congress has sought 181 seats from the SP.
"We have made up our mind on how many seats we will contest. The Samajwadi Party and the INDIA alliance will defeat the BJP together," he said, adding that the "theft" of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya will be a major poll issue.
The Uttar Pradesh Assembly has 403 seats.

title: Vaishnaw stresses need for India to make own semiconductor machinery
content:
Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday stressed the need for India to make its own machinery and high-precision components for semiconductor production, as the Centre works to build a robust domestic ecosystem for the sector.
Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Information and Broadcasting, and Railways, made the remarks during a visit to the Ethereal Machines facility in Bengaluru, the PIB in Karnataka said in a post on X.
He said the Centre, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was firmly committed to building a robust semiconductor ecosystem in the country.
"In the spirit of 'Atmanirbhar Bharat', as envisioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it is important that India develops and manufactures its own machines and high-precision components required for semiconductor manufacturing," he said.
The Ethereal Machines facility was playing an important role in this direction by producing advanced machinery and high-precision components, he said.

content:

"In my view, this can be dangerous," Zelenskyy told reporters on Friday. "This should not be the main agenda." His comments were embargoed until Saturday.
Zelenskyy also said the United States had asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas region in eastern Ukraine that Russia does not control if Kyiv were admitted to NATO.
He said he believed Moscow was interested in reopening broader questions about European security rather than focusing exclusively on ending the 4 1/2-year war.

title: Centre operationalises portal for online declaration of rice, paddy stock
content:
The government has operationalised a portal for online declaration of paddy or rice stock by all entities including traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers, a move aimed at preventing hoarding and to check prices.
As per the November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all states and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories  -- Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy.
In a social media post on Saturday, the nodal food ministry said it has operationalised the food stock declaration portal for this purpose.
As per the order, every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday.
Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

content:

title: Bhupender Yadav calls for coordinated action by NCR states on pollution
content:
Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on Saturday said air pollution does not recognise state boundaries, and called for coordinated implementation of pollution control measures across the national capital region (NCR).
The minister stressed the need for real-time monitoring through integrated command and control centres (ICCCs), and direct accountability of field officers for violations.
Yadav on Saturday chaired a meeting to assess measures undertaken in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan for mitigating air pollution in Delhi-NCR.
During the meeting, state governments were directed to nominate secretary-level officials for seven cities in Haryana, four cities in Uttar Pradesh, and four cities in Rajasthan for implementation of pollution control measures through field visits and submission of weekly reports to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).

title: Gurugram to install 300 ANPR cameras to enforce 'no PUC, no fuel' rule
content:
The Gurugram administration will be installing Automated Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras across petrol pumps in the city to monitor and enforce the 'no pollution under control (PUC) certificate, no fuel' policy, officials said on Saturday.
District Transport Officer and Secretary of the Regional Transport Authority,  Sanjeev Singla, said 300 cameras will be installed in the first phase, starting November 15.
He further said that all petrol pumps have been ordered to install warning boards prominently in both Hindi and English at entry points and fuelling areas, underlining that vehicles without PUC certificates won't be provided petrol, diesel, or CNG.
The 'no valid pollution under control (PUC) certificate, no fuel' policy was implemented across the National Capital Region on October 1.

content:
China is set to host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting next week in its high-tech Shenzhen city, where the presidents of China, the US and Russia will hold a historic trilateral summit.
The meeting of the 21-nation Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders will take place November 18-19.
It gains importance as Chinese President Xi Jinping will host a summit with his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. Discussions at the trilateral summit are expected to focus on a host of global issues, including global conflicts, AI and the reduction of nuclear weapons by big powers.
The White House confirmed that the three leaders are planning to meet on the sidelines of a summit in China next week.
The historic meeting between the leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the APEC summit in Shenzhen, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told the media.

title: NCP merger talks ended after Ajit Pawar's death, says Supriya Sule
content:
NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule on Saturday said the merger discussions between the two factions of the Nationalist Congress Party ended for her after her cousin Ajit Pawar's death, and she had not received any communication from the other side on the issue.
She also rejected speculation about her party joining the BJP-led NDA.
Sule's categorical denials came amid renewed buzz about the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) and the NCP headed by Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar reuniting.
"When my brother (then NCP chief Ajit Pawar) was alive, there were discussions about a merger. A date had also been decided. But the day my brother passed away, the merger issue came to a full stop for me and within our party," Sule told reporters.
"There has been no discussion on joining the NDA. When there has been no beginning, where does the question of a full stop arise?" she said when asked if she had also "put a full stop" to the talk of her party joining the ruling alliance at the Centre.

title: Patanjali Foods Q2 FY27 results: Net profit falls 19% to ₹420 crore
content:
Patanjali Foods Ltd on Saturday reported 19 per
cent fall in consolidated net profit at Rs 419.76 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 despite rise in revenue.
Its net profit stood at Rs 516.69 crore in the year-ago period.
Total income rose to Rs 11,406.49 crore in the second quarter of the current fiscal from Rs 9,850.06 crore a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
Total operational expenses went up to Rs 10,997.51 crore from Rs 9,344.97 crore.
During the first six months of this fiscal, the net profit rose to Rs 755.49 crore from Rs 697.05 crore in the year-ago period. Total income grew to Rs 22,748.38 crore from Rs 18,629.08 crore.
Incorporated in 1986, Patanjali Foods is one of the leading FMCG players in India.
The company is present in edible oils, FMCG, and wind power generation segments. It sells products under different brands including Patanjali, Ruchi Gold, Nutrela, Dant Kanti, Mahakosh and Sunrich.

In an interactive session at the HT Leadership Summit, the external affairs minister said the negotiations are approaching the "finishing line," adding that many of the remaining issues are "not so much at our end" and that more changes have occurred on the American side.
"Well, it's certainly our hope, and in many ways anticipation that we are at the last stretch. That's not a secret," he said responding to a question on the negotiations for the trade pact.

title: Sammaan Capital Q2 FY27 results: Net profit rises 1.25% to ₹312 crore
content:
Non-bank lender Sammaan Capital on Saturday reported a 1.25 per cent increase in its September quarter net profit to Rs 312.34 crore compared to Rs 308.47 crore in the same quarter of last year.
The company had reported a net profit of Rs 243.30 crore in the preceding June quarter.
Its total income declined to Rs 1,850.85 crore in the reporting quarter from Rs 2,260.52 crore in the year-ago period, which included a decline in the core interest income to Rs 1,161.26 crore from Rs 1,449.02 crore.
Total expenses also declined to Rs 1,426.28 crore from Rs 1,835.49 crore in the year-ago period, as per a regulatory filing.
Assets under management grew by 5 per cent to Rs 59,188 crore as of end-June 2026, driven by a 62 per cent jump in disbursements to Rs 6,278 crore. It aims to increase AUM to Rs 70,000 crore by March 2027.
The company added more branches during the quarter to take its overall network to 245 as of September 30, and is aiming to take the same to 270 by end of the fiscal

title: Bihar govt reviews Chhath festival arrangements, safety measures
content:
The Bihar government has reviewed Chhath festival arrangements, including measures to ensure the safety of devotees and steps to deal with any eventuality, an official statement said on Saturday.
The Disaster Management Department announced strict enforcement of the ban on firecracker bursting during the festival on safety grounds.
The review was done at a meeting chaired by the department's Additional Secretary Nadeemul Ghaffar Siddiqui and attended by district disaster management officers.
According to the Disaster Management Department statement, they reviewed safety arrangements for devotees at Chhath ghats, regulation of boat operations and preparedness to deal with possible emergencies during the festival.
Siddiqui urged district officials to seek assistance from 'Aapda Mitras', civil defence personnel and volunteers for any rescue operations.
District Emergency Operations Centres were also directed to remain active and function smoothly, the statement said.

title: Listing may change 'Tata way', put profits ahead of philanthropy: Noel
content:
Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata on Saturday said that listing Tata Sons will "fundamentally change" the over 150-year-old group's way of working and stressed that its largest owner will play a "constructive role" in engaging with the regulators to retain the conglomerate's unlisted character.
Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit here, Noel said while "some people" are proposing a listing for the group's holding company, he fears that enlarging the number of shareholders after a listing will shift its focus to profits from philanthropy.

title: NCRTC to introduce 8 fast Namo Bharat trains from Nov 16, cut travel time
content:
The National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) will introduce eight additional fast Namo Bharat train services during morning and evening peak hours from November 16, reducing travel time between Anand Vihar and Ghaziabad to just eight minutes, officials said.
The limited-stop trains will operate on the Delhi-Meerut corridor, covering Anand Vihar to Begumpul in 36 minutes and Ghaziabad to Begumpul in 28 minutes. The entire corridor will be covered in less than 50 minutes, NCRTC said.
The fast services will stop at only five stations -- Sarai Kale Khan, Anand Vihar, Ghaziabad, Begumpul and Modipuram -- to reduce travel time for commuters, particularly office-goers and students travelling during rush hours, it said.

title: DPIIT, commerce department authorised to issue defence industrial licences
content:
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and Department of Commerce (DoC) are the competent authorities to issue industrial licences for defence purposes, the commerce and industry ministry said.
According to an official communication from DPIIT, both departments can issue these licences under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.
It stated that the industry department can issue licences for manufacturers located outside Special Economic Zones (SEZs), while the commerce department can issue licences for manufacturers located within these zones as well as for Export Oriented Units (EOUs).
"It is reiterated that the following agencies (DPIIT and DoC) are competent to issue Industrial Licences for Defence purposes under the I (D&R) Act 1951, " DPIIT's press note said.

title: Former vice president Jagdeep Dhankhar discharged from AIIMS after 3 days
content:
Former vice president Jagdeep Dhankhar was discharged from AIIMS here on Saturday, three days after he was admitted following a collapse, family sources said.
The 75-year-old former vice president was admitted to the hospital on Wednesday after he collapsed during his morning walk and remained unconscious for a few minutes.
He was admitted to the hospital's Cardio-Neuro Centre and was under the care of the Department of Cardiology for medical evaluation and treatment.
Security personnel accompanying Dhankhar had initially taken him home in a PCR vehicle after he collapsed.
Later, he was admitted to AIIMS.

title: Delhi's AQI settles at 348 in 'very poor' category, likely to worsen

The air quality index (AQI) at 9 am stood at 348 (very poor), as compared to the 24-hour average AQI of 373 at 4 pm on Friday, according to data from the Central Board of Pollution Control (CPCB).
As per the CPCB standards, an AQI of 0-50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor', and 401-500 'severe'.
Out of the 59 air quality monitoring stations in the city, seven recorded AQI in the 'severe' category on Saturday morning.
According to forecasts by the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, the AQI is expected to deteriorate further in the next few days.

title: Flights halted at airports across US due to ATC communications problems
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centres.
The FAA notice said the ground stop was being imposed "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said there is a communications issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centres that direct planes en route between airports nationwide. He said FAA technicians are investigating. This is the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. Before that, the last time had been after the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication yet that "this was a nefarious attack against us. It's just a telecommunications outage."
"Everybody's safe. There's no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they're flying," Mullin said.
There is no timeline for restart
